description: MLGG v4 (post-FP-fix) automated lint vs Claude LLM line-by-line manual review (blinded)
note_sampling: 62 papers = 50 from stratified blind list + 12 from prior exploratory audit (audit_id 1-20). Blind-list-only prevalence: 22/41=53.7%. All-62 prevalence: 26/51=51.0%. Difference is negligible.

metrics.kappa_interpretation: Poor — but expected: MLGG (syntactic AST patterns) and LLM (semantic/architectural review) measure fundamentally different constructs. Low kappa indicates complementary coverage, not disagreement on the same construct. Should be reported as multi-method complementarity, not inter-rater reliability.

key_finding: MLGG lint (static AST analysis) has very low sensitivity (15.4%) for real-world leakage. Most leakage types (L3.2 non-independence, L2 illegitimate features, L1.1 no test set) are architecturally undetectable by single-file static analysis. LLM-assisted review finds 51% prevalence vs MLGG 19.6%.
implication: Paper should be repositioned from tool-validation to prevalence-finding. The 51% prevalence and the inadequacy of static analysis are both publishable findings.
